<h2>Thirty years of Irish tree-planting promises, checked against the record</h2>
<p>Ireland has planted a fraction of the forest it promised since 1996. Licensing explains one bad stretch. Farmers walking away from planting explains more of the gap.</p>

<h3>A map can clarify the world and still leave something out</h3>
<p>Reading James C. Scott's Seeing Like a State as a warning about simplification, and as a useful question for anyone who builds models for policy.</p>
